narrative:
The model estimates an 86% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns in your profile that strongly align with employees who tend to depart.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you received other job offers while working here, and how long you have been with this specific organization. These stood out as the strongest drivers compared with all other details the system reviewed.

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1–5 years of experience, your mid-range tenure matches people who often begin exploring new opportunities. The fact that you have received other job offers also strongly increased the likelihood of departure, as this is relatively uncommon among those expected to remain. Finally, your 1–5 years in your current role added further weight toward leaving, since shorter tenures at one organization frequently signal higher turnover risk.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of someone likely to move on. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether additional responsibilities, better recognition, or improved work-life support could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding before deciding on next steps. (248 words)
